Composition scatter: group proportions in two conditions

Source: R/composition_plots.R
plot_composition_scatter.Rd

Plots, for each group of cells (e.g. cell type or state), its proportion (or number of cells) in one condition on x against another condition on y, with the y = x line: groups above the line are more abundant in the y condition. Optionally one panel per level of `facet.by` (e.g. stage), and per-sample proportions with their mean and SEM (`sample.by`). Square panels of a fixed size; save it with save_plot; the table behind it is returned by export_source_data.

Usage

plot_composition_scatter(
  object,
  group.by,
  split.by,
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  facet.by = NULL,
  sample.by = NULL,
  error = c("sem", "sd", "ci95"),
  cells = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  value = c("percent", "count"),
  log = FALSE,
  fold.lines = NULL,
  label = TRUE,
  label.size = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  pt.size = 4,
  panel.width = 2.5,
  panel.height = panel.width,
  legend.position = "none",
  bg = "transparent"
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object, or a data frame with one row per cell (e.g. its metadata)

group.by

Column of the groups, one point each (e.g. cell state)

split.by

Column of the conditions; its levels `x` and `y` are compared on the axes (e.g. genotype)

x, y

Levels of `split.by` on the x- and y-axis. If NULL (default), the first and second level

facet.by

Column giving one panel per level (e.g. stage), with proportions computed within each. Default is NULL

sample.by

Column of the samples. If given, proportions are computed per sample and each point is the mean of the samples of a condition, with error bars on both axes (see `error`), so that every sample counts the same. If NULL (default), cells of all samples are pooled into one proportion per condition

error

Error bars with `sample.by`: "sem" (default; standard error of the mean), "sd" (standard deviation of the samples) or "ci95" (95% confidence interval of the mean, mean +- t(0.975, n - 1) x SEM). The horizontal bar is computed from the samples of the x condition, the vertical one from those of the y condition. A condition with one sample has no bar

cells

Cells (rows) to use, as names or indices, e.g. one lineage: proportions are then of that subset. If NULL (default), all

groups

Groups to draw. Proportions are still computed over all groups. If NULL (default), all

value

"percent" (default; the proportion, labelled in %) or "count" (the number of cells)

log

Whether to draw both axes on a log10 scale, default is FALSE. Spreads rare groups; groups with 0 cells in a condition cannot be drawn and are left out, with a message

fold.lines

Fold changes drawn as dashed lines around y = x, e.g. 2 draws y = 2x and y = x / 2. Default is NULL (none)

label

Which points to name (needs ggrepel): TRUE (default) for all, FALSE for none, or the groups to name. Labels of many rare groups crowd near the origin on linear axes; name a few, or use `log = TRUE`

label.size

Size of the labels in mm. If NULL (default), the small text size of the theme (9 pt)

cols

Colours of the groups: NULL (default) for the colours DimPlot_bioToolkit gives them, a qualitative palette name, or colours named by group

pt.size

Size of the points, default is 4

panel.width, panel.height

Size of each (square) panel in inches, default 2.5; `panel.height` defaults to `panel.width`

legend.position

Position of the group legend, default is "none" (points are named)

bg

Background colour, default is "transparent"

Value

A ggplot object

Details

The source data (export_source_data) hold one row per group (and panel): the values on x and y, the cell counts and totals of both conditions and, with `sample.by`, the SEM, SD, number of samples and the half-width of the error bars drawn (`x_error`, `y_error`). Per-sample proportions are returned by summarize_group_meta.

Groups with no cells in either condition (of a panel, or among `cells`) are not drawn.

The plot shows where proportions differ, not whether the difference is significant: that needs a test on samples, not cells (e.g. propeller, scCODA).

See also

summarize_group_meta, save_plot

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Pooled proportions of each cell state, WT vs Mut, one panel per stage
plot_composition_scatter(obj, group.by = "cell_state", split.by = "genotype",
                         x = "WT", y = "Mut", facet.by = "stage")

# Per-sample proportions: mean +- SEM; log axes for rare states
p <- plot_composition_scatter(obj, group.by = "cell_state", split.by = "genotype",
                              x = "WT", y = "Mut", sample.by = "sample",
                              log = TRUE, fold.lines = 2)
save_plot(p, "composition.pdf")
} # }
